widgets_values:
# Character Dataset (GPT-Image-2)

Generates a **25-image LoRA training dataset** of one character from a single photo -
24 generated shots plus the real reference tile, each with a matching caption `.txt`.
**No GPU is used**: local nodes only crop, resize and save; every generation is an API
call to `gpt-image-2`.

## Setup

**1. Pick your generator.** Two builds of this graph exist and reach the same model:

* **Codex build** (the image nodes say *Codex Image Gen*) - needs a **paid ChatGPT
  subscription**, Plus at $20/month recommended, and the **Codex CLI already logged in**
  on this machine under the same user account that runs ComfyUI:
  `codex login`
  There is no API key and no OAuth flow inside ComfyUI. Drop in the **Codex Login
  Status** node to confirm the account, plan and token expiry before spending a run.
* **Replicate build** (the image nodes say *Replicate Image Gen*) - needs a Replicate
  API key as `REPLICATE_API_TOKEN`, in your environment or a `.env` file in the ComfyUI
  root. Pasting it into the node is optional.

**2. Load your photo** into the `Load Image` node. Full-body, well-lit and front-facing
works best - the face crop is derived from it.

**3. Set NAME** - it drives every output filename and doubles as the LoRA trigger word.

**4. Set the folder name** on the Run Folder node. Each run makes a new numbered folder.

**5. Set the SUBJECT** node - gender plus any notes. This is the only place gender is
stated; all 24 prompts stay gender-neutral and inherit it from here.

## Cost - read before Run

A full run is **24 generations**, sent with 2 in flight (`run_mode = all at once`,
`max_concurrent = 2` on the shared settings node). Set that to `one at a time` if your
account rate-limits.

**Start with 2-3, not 24.** The Shot Selector's `how_many` controls this and defaults to
`first N in order`, so `3` runs the first three shots and never bills the other 21 -
unselected branches are never executed at all. `force_rerun` is off, so re-queueing an
unchanged shot does not re-bill.

## Prompts

Each of the 24 shots is a **JSON system instruction** carrying its own framing,
aesthetic, wardrobe, lighting, palette and constraints. They describe the *photograph*,
not the person - face, hair, skin and build always come from your reference image, which
is what lets one fixed prompt set work for any subject.

Three blocks are shared by all 24 (see the PROMPT TEXT group) and are where to change
global behaviour: **IDENTITY** (the likeness lock), the **SUBJECT** line, and **EXCLUDE**
(content safety, rendering realism and neutral white balance).

If you edit a shot: keep `framing` as the first key, keep the explicit crop negative on
every close-up and waist-up shot, and update its caption to match. Anything captioned is
*excluded* from what the LoRA learns, so captions describe pose, expression, wardrobe and
background - never face, hair or eye colour.

## Aspect ratio / quality

Change them once on the **Image Gen Settings** node - it is wired into the `settings`
input of all 24 image nodes and overrides their individual widgets. That node exists
because `aspect_ratio` is a COMBO and ComfyUI rejects STRING->COMBO links, so a plain
wire is impossible; the settings node passes a typed bundle instead.

widgets_values:
Subject: the SAME person shown in the reference images.

Reference roles:
Image 1: face and hair identity anchor - use it for the exact likeness.
Image 2: a wider view of the same person - use it for skin tone, build and hair length.
Do NOT copy the clothing from the references: each shot states its own Wardrobe below.

Use the references ONLY for the person's identity and appearance. Do NOT copy their crop,
camera distance, pose or background - the Framing, Scene and Lighting lines above define
this shot and always override the references.

Preserve exactly: face geometry, facial features, eye colour, eyebrows, hairline, hair
texture and colour, skin tone, distinguishing marks, and - wherever the body is visible -
the same body proportions. Do not change the face, skin tone or identity in any way. It
must be unmistakably the same person.

Match the reference's ACTUAL build: the same weight, the same width of face, neck,
shoulders and torso. Do not slim down, broaden, bulk up, lengthen, idealise or otherwise
flatter the body or the face. Do not make the jaw stronger, the neck thicker or the frame
larger than the reference shows.

nodes.title: EXCLUDE BLOCK (all 24 shots)
widgets_values:
Exclude: text, captions, watermarks, logos, borders, collage or split frames,
additional people, duplicated or malformed hands and limbs, plastic or over-smoothed skin,
heavy beauty retouching.

Content safety - applies to EVERY shot regardless of its styling: no weapons of any kind,
firearms, knives or ammunition; no alcohol, bottles, cans, glasses or drinking; no
cigarettes, cigars, vaping, smoke or drugs; no blood, injury, violence, threatening poses
or aggressive gestures; no hand signs or gestures that could read as offensive; no nudity,
underwear, swimwear or revealing clothing. The subject is always a clothed adult, and any
period or genre styling is expressed only through wardrobe, set and lighting.

Rendering - applies to EVERY shot: this must look like a real photograph taken on real
equipment, not a digital render. Keep natural skin texture with visible pores, fine lines,
uneven tone and small blemishes; natural facial asymmetry; stray flyaway hairs; fabric
that creases and hangs under its own weight; slightly uneven ambient light; gentle lens
vignetting and a natural softening toward the corners.
Avoid: airbrushed, waxy or plastic skin; flawless symmetry; a glowing rim-light traced
around every edge; over-sharpened micro-contrast; HDR halos; exaggerated specular
highlights; showroom-clean CGI surfaces; and the glossy over-produced look of an AI image.

Overall grade - applies to EVERY shot: bright, light and airy. Favour a clean whitish
base - lifted open shadows, soft neutral highlights, restrained saturation, plenty of
light and air in the frame. Even a night or interior scene stays bright and clearly lit.
Never crush the image into heavy blacks, deep vignettes or a muddy, weighty grade.

White balance - applies to EVERY shot: keep it NEUTRAL to very slightly cool. No yellow,
amber, golden, orange or sepia cast anywhere - not on skin, not on walls, not in the
highlights. Light sources read as clean white daylight or neutral studio light, never as
warm tungsten or candlelight. Whites stay white, skin stays its true tone.
Output: a single photorealistic photograph.
